candidates.body:
The same root cause also produces a spurious compile error. When the cast type is a union containing `int` and `decimal`, a floating-point literal operand is typed as float instead of decimal, and the cast is rejected as impossible:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    int|decimal x = <int|decimal>2.5;
    io:println(x); // @output 2.5
    io:println(x is decimal); // @output true
}
```

Actual:
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: impossible type conversion, intersection is empty
 --> c1.bal:4:21
```
`any y = <int|decimal>2.5;` fails the same way. `<decimal>2.5` and `<decimal|string>2.5` work.

Expected: prints `2.5` then `true`.
- §6.20: the contextually expected type of the operand is the intersection with `int|decimal`.
- §6.5: for a floating-point-literal the candidates are float and decimal. float is eliminated because its intersection with `int|decimal` is empty. So the literal is decimal `2.5`, which already belongs to the cast type.

Checked on main @ fd93c6a3f.

Spec: https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/ was fetched, but validators found it serves an older preview without group by/collect, so they cross-checked against https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/2024R1/. Many confirmed bugs were dropped as duplicates of open issues with essentially the same reproducers: #1223, #1394, #1046, #1110, #1047, #1149, #1225, #1044, #1050, #1103, #1453, #1091, #1259, #1132, #1249, #163 (match-guard call restriction), #1424, #1166, #1070, #1332, #1511, #1153. Dropped after validation: a non-Cloneable named arg (`f = function() {}`) in an error constructor. A validator called it a bug, but §5 says functions are inherently immutable, so the value is readonly and therefore Cloneable. Not pursued (weak or likely intentional): `string:indexOf("", startIndex > length)` returns the length instead of nil (jBallerina probably matches); unused function parameters, non-public module variables and constants are reported as `unused variable` errors (looks deliberate, but it is not listed under spec deviations in subset10.md); a possible minor follow-up for #1511 is that `toBalString` also ignores an object's `toString`. The workers/start/wait hunter was stopped before it reported anything.
